title: Duplicates Close to Each Other

concept.title: Remember the last position of each value
body: You need two equal values whose positions differ by at most `k`. If a value `x` occurs at positions `p1 < p2 < p3`, the closest pair among them is always **two neighbours** in this list. So it is enough to remember the **last position** of every value: when `x` appears again at position `i`, compare `i` with the stored last position.
Updating `last[x]` every time is the important part: only the most recent earlier copy can be the closest one.

statement: Given `n` integers and a number `k`, is there a pair of positions `i < j` with `a[i] = a[j]` and `j - i <= k`? Print `yes` or `no`.

examples.note: The two 1s are 3 apart, the two 2s are 3 apart: no.

hints: Equal values can be far apart in the array.
Remember the last position where each value was seen.
When a value repeats, compare the distance with k, then update the position.

explanation: Only the most recent earlier copy of a value can be its nearest one, so a map from value to last position decides the question in one pass.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

last = {}
found = False
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    if x in last and i - last[x] <= k:
        found = True
        break
    last[x] = i
print("yes" if found else "no")
